text:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: latency spike detected on inference-prod (us-east-1). p95 jumped ~80ms -> ~800ms starting 12:03 UTC. Affected: batch-serving nodes (shard ids 12-16).

maria: looking at dashboards now. kernel selection appears to be oscillating between aten_fused and custom_attn_v2 on the same set of shards. traffic pattern hasn't changed for acme-inc tenant though.

jon: recall we merged a kernel-selector heuristic yesterday that picks custom_attn_v2 for sequences >1024 and when sm_util>60%. could be that combined with a sudden occupancy bump. rollback is a fast option.

oliver: I just put a short routing pin for tenant=acme-inc to model:llama-3-small (route->fallback) to stop the spike while we triage. also set feature flag kernelselector:prefer_stable=true for that tenant.

anya: uploaded a quick profile from shard-13:```
[profile] shard=13 timeframe=12:02-12:10
kernel=custom_attn_v2 p50=28ms p95=420ms p99=670ms sm_occupancy=97% gmem_wait=42%
kernel=aten_fused p50=22ms p95=110ms p99=190ms sm_occupancy=45%
kvcache.evictions/sec: baseline~3 -> spike~210
queued_batch_size_mean: 14 -> 58
```

maria: kvcache eviction rate is wild on 12-14. looks like eviction thrash + aggressive batching = head-of-line blocking. I saw a misconfigured prefix cache TTL on a recent deploy (defaults got lowered).

jon: two quick mitigations: (1) clamp max_batch_tokens to 2048 and prefer_low_latency=true in the batching heuristic, (2) revert the kernel-selector change or add a short-circuit: if gpu_occupancy>90% avoid custom_attn_v2.

oliver: I'm applying per-tenant throttling: acme-inc QPS cap 400->200 for 15m. also toggled dynamic_batching=false for that tenant via flags service.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolled back service redwood/kernel-selector 2.14 -> 2.13 on cluster-inference-1 at 12:20 UTC by oliver. (ci build 2.13 verified)

anya: immediate effects after rollback: p95 on affected shards fell from ~420ms -> ~95ms within 90s. KV eviction still elevated but trending down. appears kernel-selector was the amplification vector.

maria: agree. still want to address KV cache TTL and eviction settings: proposal - increase kvcache_max_entries to 8k on batch-serving nodes and revert the TTL change from yesterday's config. I'll open the config PR.

jon: I'll add selector change: "if sm_occupancy>90% do not choose custom_attn_v2" + a circuit-breaker that forces aten_fused for 5m on repeat flaps. will send PR and link.

oliver: monitoring/alerts adjusted: p95 alert threshold for cluster-inference-1 temporarily lowered to 200ms while we watch. incident page open: https://internal.incidents/1775550000. will update again at 12:40 UTC.

maria: posting a short update to #incident-update and paging platform-oncall if p95 >200ms in next 10m.

anya: 25m after initial alert: p95 stable ~100ms, eviction rate down to ~8/sec after throttles + TTL revert. batching mean back to ~12. Good signal. Recommend follow-up postmortem to dig into why kernel-selector and TTL change combined to amplify the noisy-neighbor effect.

oliver: thanks all — closing this incident as mitigated for now. please join a short postmortem sync (eng-runtime + eng-ml + eng-sre) at 15:00 to capture actions. :bow:
